mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has decelerated its decline for four consecutive weeks (-52.7 to -30.7), a momentum pattern that typically persists for several more weeks as behavioral adaptation and gradual reopening continue, pushing the next-4-week mean above the last-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved monotonically from -52.7 to -30.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the last 28-day mean despite four consecutive weeks of prior improvement, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility surged from -37.3 to -6.9 over four weeks. If this surge continues past a near-baseline threshold, outdoor recreation substitutes for indoor retail/recreation trips, dampening or reversing RETAIL_REC growth over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -5 and week-on-week change exceeds 15 points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -37.3 to -6.9 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: If PARKS crosses above -5 with a large week-on-week jump and RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean still exceeds its last-4-week mean, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES (-30.7 to -23.9) and TRANSIT (-54.9 to -41.7) signals a policy-driven phased reopening that restores commuting and errand-linked retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved every week in the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue improving but RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean does not rise relative to the last-4-week mean, the policy-linkage mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT recovery combined with declining RESIDENTIAL time (14.4 to 9.4) jointly indicate reduced home confinement and restored mobility infrastructure use; their interaction amplifies discretionary outings more than either series alone, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved while RESIDENTIAL declined each week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT keeps improving and RESIDENTIAL keeps declining but RETAIL_REC's next-2-week mean fails to exceed its prior 2-week mean, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is nearing baseline (-9.9 at t-0w). Once essential-trip demand saturates near zero, the behavioral slack shifts toward discretionary retail, producing a short-term boost in RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -21.1 to -9.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -5 but RETAIL_REC's following week mean does not rise relative to the prior week, the saturation-substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has declined monotonically each week (14.4 to 9.4), reflecting a structural seasonal reduction in time spent at home; this steady unwinding mechanically frees time for short-term retail and recreation trips the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell every week from 14.4 to 9.4
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues falling but RETAIL_REC's next-week mean does not rise relative to the current week, the seasonal unwinding mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If a renewed tightening of restrictions occurs, evidenced by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT dropping sharply week-on-week, the recent recovery trend in RETAIL_REC reverses and the series declines over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES or TRANSIT drops more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:both series had been improving gradually, making a sudden drop a clear regime-change signal
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES or TRANSIT drops more than 10 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean still exceeds the prior 4-week mean, the tightening-reversal mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in PARKS and WORKPLACES indicates a broad-based normalization of both leisure and work mobility; their combined rise interacts to generate compounding behavioral confidence that raises RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks beyond what either series predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS and WORKPLACES both continue to improve but RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean does not exceed its last-4-week mean, the compounding-confidence interaction mechanism is rejected.
